title: common garden hybrids (the nine dropped by the old bare-binomial rule)

species.note: This catalog's first Chrysanthemum, and a hybrid of garden origin usually given as a complex cross with Chrysanthemum indicum among its parents (Chrysanthemum zawadskii is the other parent most sources name) — take no field from either parent's page. Expect the synonym Dendranthema × grandiflorum across older sources, and expect "Florist's Chrysanthemum", "Hardy Mum" and "Mum" in the same alphabetised common-name list; the already-landed Leucanthemum × superbum (Shasta Daisy) and Tanacetum vulgare (Tansy) are the daisies it must not borrow from. Capture the toxicity with its exact cat/dog scoping plus any separate handling/contact-dermatitis warning rather than one collapsed 'toxic'. Enum trap: ordinary moist but well-drained border soil is moderate, not fast and not moisture_retentive. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.

A sterile garden hybrid of Nepeta racemosa × Nepeta nepetella; the catalog already holds Nepeta cataria as Catnip (b8), so lead with Faassen's Catmint and let no catnip text — cat-attractant claims included — cross over from either parent or from cataria. 'Walker's Low', 'Six Hills Giant' and 'Junior Walker' are cultivar pages and cannot supply any field. Capture whatever the sources actually say about toxicity with its cat/dog scoping rather than inferring from catnip's edibility. Enum trap: it wants good drainage in ordinary soil, so reserve soil_drainage fast for a stated sharp or sandy requirement. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.

This catalog's first Calibrachoa, and a hybrid of garden origin whose parentage no admissible source publishes cleanly — say so in name_note rather than naming a parent, and borrow nothing from the already-landed Petunia × atkinsiana (b14, landed as Petunia), which is the nearest relative and the likeliest source of bleed. 'Superbells', 'Million Bells' and 'Cabaret' are trademarked cultivar series: a series page is a cultivar-only page and supports no field. Capture any non-toxic statement with its exact cat/dog scoping. Enum trap: a container plant that dries fast is not evidence of soil_drainage fast; that token needs a sharp or sandy requirement. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.

A bedding hybrid of garden origin, usually given as Verbena peruviana × Verbena phlogiflora; neither parent's page may supply a field. The live naming trap is that current treatments move it to Glandularia × hybrida — follow whichever name RHS's Name Status row and NC State's current title actually carry, record the other in name_note, and do not silently drop the hybrid sign either way. The catalog already holds Verbena hastata (American Blue Vervain, b76), a straight native species whose content must not cross over. Capture toxicity scoping exactly as stated. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.

This catalog's first Fuchsia, and a hybrid of garden origin usually given as Fuchsia magellanica × Fuchsia fulgens — both parents have their own pages and neither may supply a field, magellanica least of all, since its hardiness is routinely quoted for the whole group. Expect "Lady's Eardrops" in the common-name list. Most of what is sold is a named cultivar; a cultivar page supports nothing here. Capture any ASPCA-style non-toxic statement with its exact cat/dog scoping, and note that edible-berry statements carry conditions that must be reproduced verbatim. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.

A natural hybrid usually given as Citrus micrantha × Citrus medica, and many sources still write it without the hybrid sign as "Citrus aurantiifolia" — land it with the sign and say in name_note which spelling each source used. The catalog already holds Citrus limon (Lemon), Citrus sinensis (Orange) and Citrus reticulata (Mandarin orange), and the Persian or Tahiti lime is a DIFFERENT taxon (Citrus × latifolia); take no field from any of them. Capture the phototoxic sap/peel handling warning separately from any ingestion toxicity, with the scoping each source gives. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.

A garden hybrid of Spiraea cantoniensis × Spiraea trilobata; the catalog already holds Spiraea japonica (Japanese Spirea, b34) and Spiraea tomentosa (Steeplebush, b60), and none of those four pages may supply a field. The naming trap is the common name: "Bridalwreath Spirea" is widely applied to Spiraea prunifolia as well, so lead with Vanhoutte Spirea and disclose the shared name in name_note. Its pruning and bloom-time facts are frequently written about the genus as a whole — take only species-specific prose. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.

This catalog's first Canna, and a garden hybrid group most often traced to Canna indica and Canna glauca; sources disagree about the parentage and many file garden cannas under Canna indica or a bare "Canna generalis", so record which name each source carries in name_note and never let an indica page supply a field. Expect "Canna Lily" and "Common Garden Canna" in the same list; it is not a lily and must not pick up Lilium or Hedychium content. Capture any non-toxic-to-cats-and-dogs statement with its exact scoping. Enum trap: a stated tolerance for wet or boggy ground is moisture_retentive only when a page frames it as a cultivation requirement. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.

This catalog's first Crocosmia, a hybrid of Crocosmia aurea × Crocosmia pottsii; both parents have pages and neither may supply a field. Expect the synonyms Tritonia × crocosmiiflora and Montbretia, and note that 'Lucifer', the cultivar most sources illustrate, belongs to a different Crocosmia cross — a 'Lucifer' page is a cultivar page and supports nothing. Invasiveness and naturalisation notes are not care fields; keep them out of the record except where a source states a cultivation consequence. Capture toxicity scoping exactly as written. Confirm taxon-specific content on the dedicated page for this exact name, never a genus-level, cultivar-only, or multi-species page; for a hybrid this means the hybrid's own page, never a parent species' page.
